official_external_sources.proposition: Liability versus equity classification depends on whether the issuer has an obligation to deliver cash or another financial asset; a compound instrument is split into liability and equity components.

Preference-share classification follows the substance of contractual rights: fixed-date or holder-option cash redemption creates a liability characteristic; non-redeemable preference shares with issuer-discretionary distributions may be equity depending on the other terms.

Reacquired own equity instruments are generally deducted from equity; no gain or loss is recognised in profit or loss on purchase, sale, issue or cancellation, subject to the standard's stated exception.

Equity investments are measured at FVPL by default; IFRS 9 permits an irrevocable instrument-by-instrument OCI presentation election for eligible non-trading equity investments, and accumulated OCI is not recycled to profit or loss on derecognition.

Current-period OCI comprises items excluded from profit or loss when an IFRS requires or permits; other IFRSs determine whether and when amounts previously recognised in OCI are reclassified to profit or loss.
Control requires power, exposure or rights to variable returns and the ability to use power to affect returns; NCI is equity in a subsidiary not attributable directly or indirectly to the parent.
Profit or loss and each OCI component are attributed to owners of the parent and NCI; cumulative preference shares held by NCI require the stated dividend adjustment.
Basic EPS uses profit or loss attributable to ordinary equity holders of the parent divided by weighted-average ordinary shares, with applicable after-tax preference-share adjustments.

Hong Kong local companies moved to a mandatory no-par regime on 3 March 2014 and related concepts such as share premium were abolished for that regime; this is used only as evidence that par treatment varies by jurisdiction.

calculations.use: overstatement of the numerator if group profit is incorrectly substituted for profit attributable to owners of the parent before ordinary-share preference adjustments

limits: The slide uses the historical available-for-sale label. The proposal preserves it as course history and does not restate it as a current IFRS 9 category.

The Hong Kong no-par source is an example of jurisdictional variation only. It is not evidence that the 2019 reporting entity in the lecture was incorporated in Hong Kong or that Hong Kong law governs every example.
The proposal does not claim the complete current legal rules for holding or cancelling treasury shares in any jurisdiction.

The slide 12 source does not state whether net assets 100 are opening or closing. V2 self-test 4 explicitly adopts a note-supplied reporting-date assumption and separately explains the alternative opening-balance result of NCI 22.

The two P/E formulas are a dimensional-consistency explanation, not a claim sourced to IFRS Standards: per-share price must be paired with EPS, while total ordinary equity market value must be paired with profit attributable to ordinary equity holders of the parent.
